newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: SRI LANKA SHOWERS CRICKETERS WITH GIFTS.
newsitem.headline: SRI LANKA SHOWERS CRICKETERS WITH GIFTS.

text.p: Sri Lanka began showering its cricketers with gifts on Thursday for scoring the highest number of runs in test cricket in their drawn match against India.

A senior minister told a news conference that members of the team, which scored a record 952 for six to beat England's 59-year-old record of 903 against Australia, will be given a plot of land each in a Colombo suburb.
Media and Telecommunications Minister Mangala Samarweera said the decision was made by President Chandrika Kumaratunga and later approved by the cabinet.
Kumaratunga was a surprise visitor at Colombo's R.Premadasa stadium on Wednesday, the final day of the five-day match.
The security-conscious Kumaratunga showed up unannounced at the stadium to congratulate the players after the match was over and also brought along a huge cake.

Sanath Jayasuriya and Roshan Mahanama, who set an all time partnership record in test cricket, were given $25,000 between them by the Sri Lanka cricket board. They also received television sets from a local company.
Earlier, Sri Lanka's housing minister said he was giving Jayasuriya, who scored 340 runs but failed to beat Brian Lara's record of 375, a house.
Lara was also given a house by the Trinidad government when he hit his 375 against England three years ago.
